items.title: OpenAI shipped its first inference chip
items.oneliner: OpenAI says Jalapeno delivers up to 4.1x faster inference than Nvidia. Model companies are becoming silicon companies.

items.title: Z.ai will open Ox Alpha weights
items.oneliner: Z.ai says Ox Alpha rivals DeepSeek and will release weights. China is still pushing open model pressure upstream.

items.title: Agent memory became an architecture problem
items.oneliner: This ACM paper reframes agent memory as cost architecture. Context windows are now budget lines, not just prompts.

items.title: C2PA breaks on real Android devices
items.oneliner: Android root exploits can forge C2PA camera provenance. Authenticity standards fail fast when device trust is shaky.

items.title: Browsers exposed a new XSS angle
items.oneliner: PortSwigger found tag-name tricks that bypass assumptions in browser parsing. Sanitizers and WAFs need another audit.

items.title: Omarchy shipped with serious security holes
items.oneliner: Omarchy 4.0 reportedly allows arbitrary bash execution via notifications. Security branding is worthless without secure defaults.

items.title: AI propaganda got industrialized
items.oneliner: A fake thinktank published 124 AI-written reports in nine days. Retrieval pollution is now a geopolitical attack surface.

items.title: Apple pushed AI compute into desktops
items.oneliner: Apple's M6 and M5 Ultra bring 2nm chips and up to 80 GPU cores. Local AI just got faster and pricier.

items.title: Mold made linking meaningfully parallel
items.oneliner: The mold paper reports 2.4x to 16.1x faster linking than lld. Build latency is becoming a competitive advantage.

items.title: X moved to kill Nitter
items.oneliner: Cease and desist letters shut down Nitter and XCancel. Platform risk now includes legal removal of developer workarounds.
